_comment: TLS layer rewritten 2026-05-26 from §13 full-recapture (Owner-run pcap on Windows admin PowerShell, output at tools/fingerprint-collector/tools/fingerprint-collector/captures/openai_codex/). Codex CLI 0.128.0 currently emits TLS 1.2 ClientHello (legacy_version=0x0303, no supported_versions/psk_modes/key_share extensions, classical AES-CBC + AES-GCM cipher mix). This differs from the prior 2026-05-14 template (TLS 1.3 shape: 30 ciphers including 0x1301/02/03 + 11 extensions including ext 43/45/51). Drift cause not investigated; §13 capture is current ground truth per Truth-First. Cross-checked via mitmproxy capture on the same Owner machine (same 18-cipher / 7-ext / TLS 1.2 shape observed) — confirms this is codex_cli_rs 0.128.0's native ClientHello, not a sing-box overlay. http_layer/auth_layer fields unchanged (still source-analysis-derived, no wire HTTP capture available).

_supported_versions_note: Codex CLI 0.128.0 does NOT advertise the TLS 1.3 supported_versions extension (ext 43 absent). The value [771] reflects ClientHello.legacy_version=0x0303 (TLS 1.2 only); this is the ONLY version the client is offering, not a list of acceptable versions. Loader compatibility note: required-field validators expect non-empty; [771] is the truthful single-version representation. A future schema refactor could add a 'tls_13_supported_versions_present: false' flag to distinguish 'no extension' from 'extension present with [771]', but value-wise [771] is correct.
